content.text:
I've submitted index 28 (Sb fraction 0.816) as the best composition, with a measured EQE of 0.00127%. All five EQE measurements are used; none of the five XRD measurements were.

The whole line responds very weakly. The Mg–Sb–O phases in the database are all expected to have wide band gaps, so little of the 2.7 eV light is absorbed. That's an inference: I didn't run the band-gap model or any XRD to confirm it. Even the best reading is barely above zero, so the ranking between the two Sb-rich points rests on very small numbers.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.816 | 0.00127 |
| 26 | 0.774 | 0.00115 |
| 8 | 0.208 | 0.00026 |
| 20 | 0.613 | 0.00006 |
| 0 | 0.088 | -0.00028 (noise) |

EQE rises toward the Sb-rich end. Index 28 is the most Sb-rich composition on the line, so if EQE keeps rising it is the best available point. Index 27, between the two top points, was not measured and could be slightly higher.
